description: The U.S. Life Cycle Inventory Database is a public inventory of energy and material flows for producing materials, components and assemblies in the United States, created by the laboratory now named the National Laboratory of the Rockies and its partners for life cycle assessment practitioners. It is published through the Federal LCA Commons, an interagency repository formalised by a memorandum of understanding between the US Departments of Agriculture and Energy and the Environmental Protection Agency. Coverage: United States; gate-to-gate, cradle-to-gate and cradle-to-grave unit processes for commonly used materials, products and processes, with the NETL Electricity Baseline added as a library in 2024 and, in release v1.2026-06.0, new oil and gas field combustion processes (diesel engines, gas turbines). Releases are quarterly on the federal fiscal calendar, with archives from FY17.Q4. Format and access: browse and download on the LCA Commons collaboration server, and release archives in JSON-LD, openLCA zolca, ecoSpold2 and ILCD linked from the uslci-content GitHub repository, whose wiki holds a submission handbook and change log; free. Licence: the GitHub repository carries an MIT licence; no licence for the database itself was found on the pages read, and the NLR page gives a citation format. Caveats: the provider notes that ILCD and ecoSpold exports lose some metadata, and that JSON-LD is the most complete format. Simulation uses: embodied energy and emissions factors for infrastructure materials, energy supply and waste treatment in planning and optimisation studies. Related records: the inventory is built for openLCA (platform-openlca).
